mainTopic: An ארוסה and תרומה: עולא vs. רב שמואל בר רב יהודה, אביי's limits on רבי טרפון and רבי עקיבא, the יבם, and the משנה ראשונה
overview: This amud opens with the end of a ברייתא about selling a slave. Small flaws in a slave do not cancel the sale, and big flaws are publicly known, so סימפון is not a worry with slaves. The גמרא then asks how עולא differs from רב שמואל בר רב יהודה. עולא worries about wine in her father's house, and רב שמואל בר רב יהודה worries about סימפון. The answer is that they differ in the cases of קיבל, מסר and הלך. Next, אביי limits the argument between רבי טרפון and רבי עקיבא about feeding a betrothed woman תרומה: it covers only a בת כהן and only an ארוסה. A ברייתא supports him and adds more opinions, and רבי יהודה and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל differ only over the effort of selling תרומה. The גמרא then explains from the פסוק 'קנין כספו' why a יבם does not let his יבמה eat תרומה. It also explains that the משנה orders its cases as 'זו ואין צריך לומר זו'. Finally, it gives סימפון as the reason the later משנה delays תרומה until the חופה. It begins to check this against עולא's view, and the challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A gambler slave: the buyer is stuck with the sale
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends: if the slave turns out to be a gambler, the sale stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the slave turns out to be a gambler, the sale has 'reached him': the buyer must keep the slave.
steps.whatsHappening: We are hearing the last words of a ברייתא about a slave who was sold and then turned out to be a thief or a gambler. The ruling is that the buyer is stuck with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are hidden flaws, yet they do not cancel the sale, because such traits are common in slaves. This shows that with slaves there is no real worry of סימפון, a hidden blemish that undoes the deal.

keyTerms.meaning: A gambler (someone who plays dice)
It has reached him: the buyer is stuck with the deal
A hidden flaw that could cancel a deal

phrases.english: A gambler: it has reached him.
phrases.notes: This is the end of a ברייתא that began on the previous daf: a slave who turns out to be a thief or gambler.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא brought before this section on whether סימפון applies to slaves.
steps.raayaObject: That סימפון is not a concern when buying slaves
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: a slave found to be a thief or gambler stays sold

steps.title: Serious flaws are publicly known, so slaves have no real סימפון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what flaw could still cancel a slave sale. An armed bandit or a man condemned by the king would, but those flaws are well known.
steps.simpleTranslation: What flaw is left that could cancel the sale? An armed bandit, or someone the government has sentenced to death. But those things are publicly known, so the buyer knew and accepted them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks itself whether any hidden flaw remains that could cancel a slave sale. It answers that even the serious ones are well known.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being an armed bandit or condemned to death is serious enough to cancel a sale. But such things 'have a voice': everyone hears about them. So the buyer is assumed to have known, and the sale stands. The conclusion is that slaves never really have a סימפון problem.

keyTerms.meaning: An armed bandit
Written up by the government: sentenced to death
They have a voice: the matter is publicly known

steps.whatToRemember: With slaves, small flaws don't cancel a sale and big flaws are publicly known. So סימפון is not a worry for slaves.

phrases.english: What is there?
phrases.notes: He means: what flaw is left that could cancel the sale?

phrases.english: An armed bandit or one sentenced by the government;
those things have a voice (are publicly known).

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִיכָּא לִסְטִים מְזוּיָּין אוֹ מוּכְתָּב לַמַּלְכוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the point of the ברייתא: no flaw in a slave truly cancels a sale.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Flaws that would cancel a slave sale are publicly known, so the sale is never undone. סימפון does not apply to slaves.

steps.title: What is the difference between עולא and רב שמואל בר רב יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: Both opinions agree that an ארוסה does not eat תרומה, so the גמרא asks what practical difference there is between them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, according to both Sages she does not eat תרומה. So what is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the two reasons why an ארוסה בת ישראל may not eat תרומה. It asks where the two reasons would actually lead to different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא's reason is that, while still in her father's house, someone might pour her a cup of תרומה wine and she might give it to her brothers and sisters. רב שמואל בר רב יהודה's reason is the worry of סימפון: a hidden blemish might cancel the קידושין. Since both reach the same result, the גמרא looks for a case where the two reasons split.

keyTerms.meaning: Now then / after all (opens a reasoning question)
Both according to this Sage and according to that Sage
What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: Now, both according to this master and according to that master,
phrases.notes: The two masters are עולא and רב שמואל בר רב יהודה, from the previous daf.

phrases.english: she does not eat; what is the difference between them?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדִי בֵּין לְמָר וּבֵין לְמָר לָא אָכְלָה מַאי בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the slave side-discussion and returns to the two reasons for not feeding an ארוסה תרומה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical case where עולא and רב שמואל בר רב יהודה would rule differently

steps.title: The difference: he accepted her flaws, or she was handed over
steps.stepSummary: The two opinions differ when the husband accepted her blemishes (קיבל), or when she was handed over to his agents (מסר), or went with them (הלך).
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is in cases of 'he accepted,' 'he handed over,' and 'he went.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two reasons split in specific situations. Each situation removes one worry but not the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קיבל: the husband accepted any blemishes she has. There is no more סימפון worry, so רב שמואל בר רב יהודה would let her eat, but she is still home with her siblings, so עולא would not. מסר or הלך: the father handed her over to the husband's agents, or his own agents went along with them. Now she is away from her family, so עולא would let her eat, but the סימפון worry remains, so רב שמואל בר רב יהודה would not.

keyTerms.meaning: He accepted: the husband agreed to accept any blemishes
He handed over: the father gave her to the husband's agents
He went: the father's agents went along with the husband's agents

steps.whatToRemember: עולא worries about her siblings in her father's house. רב שמואל בר רב יהודה worries about סימפון. קיבל removes only the סימפון worry; מסר and הלך remove only the sibling worry.
steps.confusionAlert: The two reasons give opposite results in these cases. In קיבל, only רב שמואל בר רב יהודה lets her eat. In מסר or הלך, only עולא lets her eat.

phrases.english: There is between them: he accepted, he handed over, and he went.
phrases.notes: 'Accepted' means the husband accepted her blemishes. 'Handed over' and 'went' mean she has left her father's house with the husband's agents.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: קיבל removes the סימפון worry but not the sibling worry. מסר and הלך remove the sibling worry but not the סימפון worry.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: רבי טרפון says all תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: רבי טרפון says a כהן may feed his betrothed entirely from תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טרפון says: they give her everything as תרומה, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting the משנה's argument. This sets up אביי's comments that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה deals with an ארוסה whose wedding date has passed, so the כהן she is engaged to must support her. רבי טרפון says all her food may be תרומה. רבי עקיבא, hinted at by 'וכו׳', says half must be חולין.

keyTerms.meaning: The holy portion of produce that only כהנים and their households may eat
And so on: the rest of the quote, here רבי עקיבא's view

phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon says:
They give her everything as teruma, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר נוֹתְנִין לָהּ הַכֹּל תְּרוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section on the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי טרפון: a betrothed woman may be fed entirely from תרומה. רבי עקיבא: half חולין, half תרומה.

steps.title: אביי: the argument is only about a בת כהן
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the מחלוקת is only about a כהן's daughter engaged to a כהן. For a בת ישראל engaged to a כהן, everyone agrees on half חולין and half תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: the argument is about a כהן's daughter engaged to a כהן. But with an Israelite's daughter engaged to a כהן, everyone agrees: half חולין and half תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי narrows the משנה's argument to one kind of woman. For the other kind, he says there is no argument at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בת כהן grew up with תרומה and knows how to keep it pure, so רבי טרפון can allow all תרומה for her. A בת ישראל is not used to these rules and might make the תרומה impure. So even רבי טרפון agrees she needs half חולין.

keyTerms.meaning: The argument (here, between רבי טרפון and רבי עקיבא)
The daughter of a כהן
Everyone agrees
Ordinary, non-holy food

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The dispute is about a priest's daughter engaged to a priest,
but with an Israelite's daughter engaged to a priest,

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל מֶחֱצָה חוּלִּין וּמֶחֱצָה תְּרוּמָה.
phrases.english: all agree: half non-holy food and half teruma.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי מַחְלוֹקֶת בְּבַת כֹּהֵן לְכֹהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the scope of the משנה quoted in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מחלוקת applies only to a בת כהן. For a בת ישראל engaged to a כהן, all agree: half חולין, half תרומה.

steps.title: אביי: the argument is only about an ארוסה, not a married woman
steps.stepSummary: אביי adds that the מחלוקת is only about an engaged woman. For a married woman, everyone agrees on half חולין and half תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי also said: the argument is about an engaged woman. But with a married woman, everyone agrees: half חולין and half תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a second limit on the same argument. It does not apply once the couple is actually married.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wife living with her husband should not have to go to the trouble of trading תרומה to get ordinary food. So for a נשואה, even רבי טרפון agrees she gets half חולין. The argument is left only for the in-between stage of an ארוסה.

keyTerms.meaning: A betrothed woman (after קידושין, before the wedding)
A fully married woman
Half

steps.whatToRemember: אביי limits the רבי טרפון / רבי עקיבא argument twice. It covers only a בת כהן, and only an ארוסה. In every other case, all agree: half חולין, half תרומה.

phrases.english: And Abaye said:
The dispute is about a betrothed woman,
but with a married woman,

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל מֶחֱצָה חוּלִּין וּמֶחֱצָה תְּרוּמָה.
phrases.english: all agree: half non-holy food and half teruma.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second limit by אביי on the same מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מחלוקת applies only to an ארוסה. For a נשואה, all agree: half חולין, half תרומה.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports both of אביי's limits
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records the מחלוקת of רבי טרפון and רבי עקיבא and limits it the same two ways אביי did.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this. רבי טרפון says she may be given everything as תרומה, and רבי עקיבא says half חולין and half תרומה. This argument is only about a כהן's daughter engaged to a כהן. For a בת ישראל engaged to a כהן, everyone agrees it is half and half. It is also only about an engaged woman. For a married woman, everyone agrees it is half and half.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what אביי said in steps 6 and 7, so it supports him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי gave two limits to the מחלוקת: it only applies to a כהן's daughter, and it only applies to an ארוסה. The ברייתא states both limits using the phrase בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים. So אביי's statements match an earlier teaching and were not just his own idea.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also taught this way in a ברייתא. This phrase brings support for what was just said.
In what case are these words said? This phrase limits a ruling to a specific case.
Everyone agrees
Half regular food and half תרומה
A fully married woman, as opposed to an ארוסה

phrases.english: It is also taught this way:
Rabbi Tarfon says:
We may give her everything as terumah.
Rabbi Akiva says:
Half non-sacred food and half terumah.
In what case are these words said?
With a priest's daughter engaged to a priest,
but with an Israelite's daughter engaged to a priest

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל מֶחֱצָה חוּלִּין וּמֶחֱצָה תְּרוּמָה.
phrases.english: everyone agrees: half non-sacred food and half terumah.
In what case are these words said?
With an engaged woman,
but with a married woman

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל מֶחֱצָה חוּלִּין וּמֶחֱצָה תְּרוּמָה.
phrases.english: everyone agrees: half non-sacred food and half terumah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's two limits from steps 6 and 7 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's limits: the מחלוקת applies only to a כהן's daughter and only to an ארוסה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that states both limits explicitly.

steps.title: רבי יהודה בן בתירא: two parts תרומה, one part חולין
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues with a third opinion: two-thirds תרומה and one-third חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בן בתירא says: we give her two parts תרומה and one part חולין.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds another opinion that falls between רבי טרפון and רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי טרפון allows all תרומה and רבי עקיבא requires half חולין. רבי יהודה בן בתירא takes a middle path: only one-third has to be חולין.

keyTerms.meaning: Parts or portions
Two parts out of three

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says:

phrases.aramaic: נוֹתְנִין לָהּ שְׁתֵּי יָדוֹת שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה,
phrases.english: We give her two parts of terumah,
and one part of non-sacred food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with an additional opinion.

steps.title: רבי יהודה and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: all תרומה, but enough to trade
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says he may give all תרומה, as long as she can sell it to buy חולין. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says she gets double the amount in תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: he gives her everything as תרומה, and she sells it and buys חולין with the money. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: wherever תרומה was mentioned, we give her double what she would get in חולין.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with two more opinions. Both let the husband give all תרומה, but they make sure she can turn it into regular food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תרומה is worth less than חולין because few people may eat it. רבי יהודה requires enough תרומה so that selling it buys her the חולין she needs. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל goes further and gives her double, so she can sell it cheaply and easily.

keyTerms.meaning: She sells and buys
Money, the value received from a sale
Double
Was mentioned

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה here is a different תנא from רבי יהודה בן בתירא in the previous step. Don't mix them up.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
He gives her everything as terumah,
and she sells it and buys
non-sacred food with the money.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Wherever terumah was mentioned,
we give her double what she would get in non-sacred food.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: נוֹתֵן לָהּ הַכֹּל תְּרוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא with two more opinions, which the next step compares.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: all תרומה, enough to sell for the needed חולין. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: double the amount in תרומה.

steps.title: How do רבי יהודה and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל differ?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the practical difference is between the last two opinions.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי יהודה and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל really differ, since both let her trade תרומה for regular food. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions seem to reach the same goal: she ends up able to buy enough חולין. So the גמרא wants to know what actually changes between them.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?
phrases.notes: "Them" means רבי יהודה and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל from the last step.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the two opinions just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical difference between רבי יהודה and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.title: The difference is the effort of selling
steps.stepSummary: They differ over effort: whether she must work hard to sell the תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is the effort.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two opinions differ over how much trouble she has to go through to sell the תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, she gets תרומה worth exactly what she needs, so she has to work to find buyers at a full price. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל gives her extra so she can sell it cheaply and quickly, which saves her that effort.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
Effort or trouble

steps.whatToRemember: All the opinions in the ברייתא try to make sure the woman ends up with enough usable food. The question is how much תרומה can replace חולין, and who carries the burden of selling it.

phrases.english: The difference between them is the effort.
phrases.notes: The effort is the work of finding buyers for the תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They differ over the effort of selling. רבי יהודה makes her work to sell at full value, while רבן שמעון בן גמליאל gives extra to spare her that trouble.

steps.title: The משנה: a יבם does not let her eat תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: a יבם does not enable the יבמה to eat תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The יבם does not let her eat תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה. This sets up the question of why it is so.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the topic was a husband's own ארוסה. Now the case is a widow waiting for ייבום with a יבם who is a כהן, and the משנה rules that she may not eat תרומה because of him.

keyTerms.meaning: The brother of a man who died childless, who is to marry the widow
Enables her to eat תרומה

phrases.english: The yavam does not enable her to eat terumah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A יבם does not enable the יבמה to eat תרומה.

steps.title: What is the reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule about the יבם.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the יבם doesn't let her eat תרומה. This prepares for the answer from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She is already tied to him by the bond of ייבום, so you might expect her to eat. The גמרא wants to know what stops it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for why a יבם does not let her eat תרומה.

steps.title: She is his brother's acquisition, not his
steps.stepSummary: The Torah allows קנין כספו to eat, but the יבמה was acquired by his brother, not by him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah says "the acquisition of his money" may eat תרומה, and this woman is his brother's acquisition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from a פסוק: only someone the כהן himself acquired may eat תרומה, and the יבמה was acquired by his brother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of קנין כספו requires the כהן's own act of acquiring. The bond between the יבם and the יבמה comes from the dead brother's marriage, not from anything the יבם did. Until the יבם completes ייבום, she is not his own acquisition, so she cannot eat.

keyTerms.meaning: The acquisition of his money, the source for who may eat a כהן's תרומה
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
His brother's acquisition

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that eating תרומה through a כהן depends on the כהן's own acquisition, not just on a family connection to him.

phrases.english: "The acquisition of his money," the Torah said,
and this one is his brother's acquisition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק requires the כהן's own acquisition (קנין כספו), but the יבמה is his brother's acquisition.

steps.title: Quoting the case of six months with the husband
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: she spent six months under the husband (and six under the יבם).
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: she completed six months under the husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה to set up a question about it. Nothing is being argued yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists three cases that do not let the woman eat תרומה. In the first, the twelve months of waiting were split half with the husband and half with the יבם. In the second, they were almost all with the husband, and in the third, almost all with the יבם. The גמרא is about to ask about the order of these cases.

keyTerms.meaning: Under the husband, while waiting for the husband to marry her
Six months

phrases.english: She completed six months under the husband.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה after explaining the rule about the יבם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Twelve months divided between the husband and the יבם, or spent mostly with either one, do not entitle her to eat תרומה.

steps.title: Why mention the יבם case at all?
steps.stepSummary: If time spent mostly with the husband does not help her, it is obvious that time with the יבם does not help either.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you said even 'under the husband' does not let her eat, do you need to say it about 'under the יבם'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the משנה. The last case seems unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband is the one who actually acquired her, while the יבם never acquired her (step 15). So if the stronger case, the husband, does not let her eat תרומה, the weaker case, the יבם, surely does not. That makes the יבם case look like it adds nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, meaning 'now that we already know...'
Is it needed? A sign that something seems obvious

phrases.english: Now, under the husband you said no,
under the יבם, is it necessary to say?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא בִּפְנֵי הַבַּעַל אָמְרַתְּ לָא, בִּפְנֵי הַיָּבָם מִיבַּעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the order of the cases just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's listing of the 'mostly with the יבם' case after the husband case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Logic from the stronger case to the weaker one (like a קל וחומר): if the husband's time does not help, the יבם's time certainly does not, so the extra case is pointless.

steps.title: The משנה uses the style 'this, and needless to say that'
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states the case that is less obvious first, then adds the obvious one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה teaches in the style of 'this, and it is not necessary to say that.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is not repeating itself pointlessly. It is following a known teaching style.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sometimes a משנה lists a case and then adds an even more obvious case, just to complete the picture. The answer accepts that the יבם case really is obvious. It explains that obvious cases are sometimes listed on purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This, and needless to say that': listing the less obvious case first, then the obvious one
It teaches, meaning the תנא presents it this way

steps.whatToRemember: A משנה can list cases from less obvious to more obvious. This is called 'זו ואין צריך לומר זו'.

phrases.english: It teaches: 'this, and it is unnecessary to say that.'

steps.triggerLanguage: זוֹ וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר זוֹ קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about the extra case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the משנה's style of presentation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The יבם case seemed to be a pointless repetition.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is intentionally added as the obvious case, in a 'this, and needless to say that' order.

steps.title: Quoting 'this was the first version of the משנה'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's statement that the earlier ruling was the משנה ראשונה. In the later version, she cannot eat תרומה until חופה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the first version of the משנה, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the משנה to set up a question about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier version, an ארוסה could eat תרומה once her wedding date arrived, even while still in her father's house. A later בית דין changed this so that she may not eat until she enters the חופה. The גמרא will now ask why.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, earlier version of the ruling, later changed
Etc., meaning the rest of the quote is understood

phrases.english: This is the first version of the משנה, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the later version, an ארוסה does not eat תרומה until she enters the חופה.

steps.title: Why did the later version change the rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the later ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the later בית דין stopped her from eating תרומה before the חופה. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once her wedding date has come, the husband is responsible for supporting her, so she seemed fit to eat his תרומה. The question is what worry made the later sages delay this until the חופה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ruling just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the later משנה forbids תרומה until חופה.

steps.title: The reason: fear of a hidden flaw that cancels the marriage
steps.stepSummary: עולא (or רב שמואל בר יהודה) says the worry is סימפון. A hidden flaw might be found that cancels the קידושין, and it would turn out she ate תרומה when she was not allowed to.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said, and some say רב שמואל בר יהודה said: because of סימפון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason for the later ruling: concern about סימפון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the חופה, the husband has not yet seen whether she has a hidden blemish. If he finds one, the קידושין may be cancelled as a mistake. Then she was never really his wife, and she ate תרומה forbidden to her. After the חופה, he has accepted her, so this worry goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: A flaw that cancels the קידושין, here a hidden blemish found in the bride

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר עוּלָּא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: עולא said, and some say רב שמואל בר יהודה:
Because of סימפון.
phrases.notes: The worry is that he may find a blemish in her, cancel the marriage, and then she will have eaten תרומה she wasn't allowed to.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of the reason.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The later ruling is due to the concern of סימפון, a blemish that would cancel the marriage.

steps.title: For עולא, each ruling has its own reason
steps.stepSummary: For עולא, the first ruling was based on the worry about a cup of wine in her father's house, and the later ruling is based on סימפון. Each ruling has a different reason. The other view will be questioned next.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for עולא: the first ruling is out of concern that they might pour her a cup in her father's house, and the later ruling is because of סימפון.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא shows that עולא's view fits smoothly, getting ready to ask a question on רב שמואל בר יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the סוגיא, עולא explained the first ruling (no תרומה right after אירוסין) as a worry that in her father's house she might be poured תרומה wine. The later change needs a new reason, and for him that is סימפון. The words 'בשלמא' signal that the next question will be: what about the other view?

keyTerms.meaning: It works well for..., which sets up a contrast with another view
The first ruling
The later ruling
Lest they pour her a cup of תרומה wine

steps.confusionAlert: This line does not finish the argument. 'בשלמא' is only the first half of a challenge, and the question on the other view comes right after.

phrases.english: Granted, according to עולא,

phrases.aramaic: קַמַּיְיתָא שֶׁמָּא יִמְזְגוּ לָהּ כּוֹס בְּבֵית אָבִיהָ,
phrases.english: the first ruling is lest they pour her a cup in her father's house,
and the later ruling is because of סימפון.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Checks the answer against each אמורא's earlier reasoning, beginning with עולא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of רב שמואל בר יהודה (the challenge is completed in the next lines).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup: for עולא, the two rulings rest on two different reasons. The next step will ask whether the other view can explain the change in the same way.
